sections.heading: What is the Past Tense?
paragraphs: In Hungarian, the past tense (múlt idő) is used to describe actions that happened in the past.
Verbs get special endings to show past time and who performed the action.

sections.heading: Affirmative – Past Tense (tanul = to study)
paragraphs: Here are the basic affirmative forms of the verb “tanul” in the past tense.

sections.heading: Negative – Past Tense (tanul = to study)
paragraphs: Negatives are formed by adding “nem” before the verb.

sections.heading: Question – Past Tense (tanul = to study)
paragraphs: Questions are formed with intonation or a question mark—no helper verb like “did” is needed.

sections.heading: Important Points
list: Hungarian normally does not require pronouns (én, te, ő...) because the verb ending shows who did the action.
Negatives are formed by adding “nem” before the verb.
Questions are formed by changing intonation or adding a question mark—no auxiliary verb like “did” is needed.

sections.heading: Examples
list: Én reggel kávét ittam. (I drank coffee in the morning.)
Ő Budapesten élt. (He/She lived in Budapest.)
Mi minden nap sportoltunk. (We exercised every day.)
Ők a parkban sétáltak. (They walked in the park.)
